title: CharacterGPT: A Persona Reconstruction Framework for Role-Playing Agents
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 3: Industry Track)
abstract_summary: CharacterGPT incrementally reconstructs character profiles from chapter summaries as a story unfolds.
verification_notes: Added after expansion; arXiv v1 2024-05-30 and NAACL industry publication 2025-04, so first-public year is 2024. It does not directly measure skills in unseen situations.

title: Revealing and Mitigating the Challenge of Detecting Character Knowledge Errors in LLM Role-Playing
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
abstract_summary: RoleKE-Bench separates errors in knowledge a character should know from errors beyond the character's cognition and evaluates correction, doubt, and refusal.
verification_notes: Added after expansion; arXiv v1 2024-09-18 and EMNLP publication 2025-11, so first-public year is 2024. It tests knowledge errors rather than practical skill.

title: RoleBreak: Character Hallucination as a Jailbreak Attack in Role-Playing Systems
venue: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Computational Linguistics
abstract_summary: RoleBreak attributes role hallucinations to sparse queries and role-query conflict and tests Narrator Mode against refusal-based handling.
verification_notes: Added after expansion; arXiv v1 2024-09-25 and COLING publication 2025-01, so first-public year is 2024. The preprint includes Jijun Zhang; the final publication does not.

title: Tell Me What You Don’t Know: Enhancing Refusal Capabilities of Role-Playing Agents via Representation Space Analysis and Editing
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
abstract_summary: Tests contextual and parametric knowledge conflicts and uses representation editing to improve role-consistent refusal.
verification_notes: Listed in 2025 seed, but arXiv v1 appeared 2024-09-25, so first-public year is 2024. The final paper adds Changze Lv to the earlier author list. This studies knowledge, not social skill.

title: CharacterBox: Evaluating the Role-Playing Capabilities of LLMs in Text-Based Virtual Worlds
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
abstract_summary: CharacterBox creates situation-specific behavior trajectories in a text virtual world with character and narrator agents, allowing trajectory-level assessment.
verification_notes: Listed in 2025 seed, but arXiv v1 appeared 2024-12-07, so first-public year is 2024; NAACL publication 2025-04.

title: RAIDEN Benchmark: Evaluating Role-playing Conversational Agents with Measurement-Driven Custom Dialogues
venue: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Computational Linguistics
abstract_summary: RAIDEN uses multi-turn annotator dialogue across 135 roles and pairwise comparison at different conversation stages.
verification_notes: Added after expansion; COLING publication 2025-01, with no earlier original release verified. The PDF includes role-cognition boundary and scene-action dimensions; source evidence is still needed per character.

title: MIRAGE: Exploring How Large Language Models Perform in Complex Social Interactive Environments
venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 2: Short Papers)
abstract_summary: MIRAGE uses eight murder-mystery scenarios to assess trust changes, clue investigation, interaction, and script compliance.
verification_notes: Added after expansion; ACL publication 2025-07 and arXiv v1 2025-01-03. Generic game skill does not determine any established character's social ceiling.

title: CoSER: Coordinating LLM-Based Persona Simulation of Established Roles
venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 267)
abstract_summary: CoSER supplies established literary characters, dialogue, experiences, thoughts, and scene conditions for given-circumstance acting and evaluation.
verification_notes: PMLR official version 2025-07; arXiv v1 2025-02-13. A 2026-01 arXiv revision changed the title. The 2025 ICML title and author order are used.

title: RoleMRC: A Fine-Grained Composite Benchmark for Role-Playing and Instruction-Following
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
abstract_summary: RoleMRC tests response, refusal, and attempted response under role ability limits in multi-turn chat, reading comprehension, and nested instructions.
verification_notes: ACL publication 2025-07; arXiv v1 2025-02-17. Task-defined ability limits do not establish a source character's actual skill ceiling.

title: Towards a Design Guideline for RPA Evaluation: A Survey of Large Language Model-Based Role-Playing Agents
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
abstract_summary: Systematic review of role-playing agent evaluation, organizing agent attributes, task attributes, and evaluation metrics into design guidance.
verification_notes: ACL publication 2025-07; arXiv v1 2025-02-18. The preprint author list included Yanfang Ye; the final ACL list is used.

title: Reasoning Does Not Necessarily Improve Role-Playing Ability
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
abstract_summary: Compares direct role-play, chain-of-thought, and reasoning-optimized models across several role-play benchmarks; generic reasoning enhancements may reduce measured role fidelity.
verification_notes: ACL publication 2025-07; arXiv v1 2025-02-24. Conclusions are bounded by the tested models and benchmarks.

title: Guess What I am Thinking: A Benchmark for Inner Thought Reasoning of Role-Playing Language Agents
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
abstract_summary: ROLETHINK tests character inner-thought inference from literature; MIRROR retrieves memories, predicts reactions, and synthesizes motivations.
verification_notes: EMNLP publication 2025-11; arXiv v1 2025-03-11. Matching thoughts is distinct from choosing actions in unseen situations.

title: Enhancing Persona Consistency for LLMs’ Role-Playing using Persona-Aware Contrastive Learning
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
abstract_summary: Persona-Aware Contrastive Learning uses role-conditioned self-questioning and contrastive alignment to improve measured persona consistency in dialogue.
verification_notes: ACL publication 2025-07; arXiv v1 2025-03-22. Improving persona consistency does not demonstrate a complete source character or ability limits.

title: EmoCharacter: Evaluating the Emotional Fidelity of Role-Playing Agents in Dialogues
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
abstract_summary: EmoCharacter measures fidelity of a character's emotional responses in single- and multi-turn dialogue; common role-play methods do not consistently improve this dimension.
verification_notes: NAACL publication 2025-04. No earlier original release verified; first-public date uses earliest verified month. Emotional fidelity is distinct from a character's limited ability to comfort someone.

title: DMT-RoleBench: A Dynamic Multi-Turn Dialogue Based Benchmark for Role-Playing Evaluation of Large Language Model and Agent
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 39(24)
abstract_summary: DMT-RoleBench evaluates six role types in dynamic multi-turn dialogue; its intents separately test knowledge boundaries, professional skill, and game interaction.
verification_notes: Added after expansion; AAAI official publication date 2025-04-11. Its PDF Table 1 distinguishes Knowledge Boundary Eval, Professional Skill Eval, and Game Interaction Eval. Professional occupations are not a direct measure of a particular fictional character's source-grounded skill ceiling.

title: RolePlot: A Systematic Framework for Evaluating and Enhancing the Plot-Progression Capabilities of Role-Playing Agents
venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
abstract_summary: RolePlot detects dialogue cues for plot progression and prompts role agents to advance literary or synthetic narratives.
verification_notes: Only ACL publication 2025-07 verified; first-public date uses earliest verified month. Plot advancement and source-character action limits require separate evaluation.

title: Do Role-Playing Agents Practice What They Preach? Belief-Behavior Consistency in LLM-Based Simulations of Human Trust
venue: arXiv preprint
abstract_summary: A Trust Game study tests whether stated beliefs predict role-playing agents' later actions and finds systematic belief-behavior gaps.
verification_notes: arXiv v1 2025-07-02. The study simulates human trust behavior rather than a fixed fictional character; it informs value-action consistency testing.

title: Persona Vectors: Monitoring and Controlling Character Traits in Language Models
venue: arXiv preprint
abstract_summary: Persona Vectors identifies activation directions for individual traits such as sycophancy and hallucination and uses them to monitor or steer model behavior.
verification_notes: arXiv v1 2025-07-29. The study concerns generic assistant traits; single-trait steering is not full established-character simulation.

title: PersonaEval: Are LLM Evaluators Human Enough to Judge Role-Play?
venue: COLM 2025
abstract_summary: PersonaEval compares LLM and human identification of speakers in human-written novels, scripts, and video dialogues.
verification_notes: arXiv v1 2025-08-06; COLM 2025 acceptance verified on the official accepted-papers list, without an exact posting date. Role identification alone cannot score all aspects of generated behavior. OpenReview PDF returned HTTP 403 to a non-browser HEAD request; the legal arXiv PDF is the primary download URL, while the formal link is retained.

title: CPO: Addressing Reward Ambiguity in Role-playing Dialogue via Comparative Policy Optimization
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
abstract_summary: CPO trains with comparative rewards for open role-play dialogue; CharacterArena compares contextual multi-turn trajectories.
verification_notes: EMNLP publication 2025-11; arXiv v1 2025-08-12. Preprint first author is Xinge Ye; final PDF says Jing Ye, which is used here. Benchmark gains do not establish faithful awkward social reactions.

title: R-CHAR: A Metacognition-Driven Framework for Role-Playing in Large Language Models
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
abstract_summary: R-CHAR uses adaptive, role-consistent reasoning trajectories and reports improvements on SocialBench social interaction tasks.
verification_notes: Only EMNLP publication 2025-11 verified; first-public date uses earliest verified month. Final-author spelling is KeZhong Lu.

title: TailorRPA: A Retrieval-Based Framework for Eliciting Personalized and Coherent Role-Playing Agents in General Domain
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
abstract_summary: TailorRPA retrieves fine-grained character memories and protective queries to reduce knowledge-boundary violations in general-domain dialogue.
verification_notes: Only EMNLP publication 2025-11 verified; first-public date uses earliest verified month. Mainly addresses knowledge boundaries.

title: CharacterCraft: Bridging the Literature-Reality Dialogue Gap for Practical Role-Playing Agents
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
abstract_summary: CharacterCraft adapts Chinese novel dialogue toward everyday user queries and uses memory retrieval for character-aligned response.
verification_notes: Added after expansion; only EMNLP publication 2025-11 verified. Focuses on dialogue distribution and memory, with limited evidence for ability ceilings.
